control.authors: Emily C Britt, Xin Qing, James A Votava et al.
control.title: Activation induces shift in nutrient utilization that differentially impacts cell functions in human neutrophils.
control.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
control.claim_basis: The abstract reports resting neutrophil reliance on glycogen, an activation-linked switch to extracellular glucose enabled by GLUT1, and function-specific consequences.
abstract_support_excerpts: Human peripheral blood neutrophils, in contrast to a neutrophil-like cell line, rely on glycogen storage as a major metabolic source under resting state but rapidly switch to primarily using extracellular glucose upon activation with various stimuli.
This shift is driven by a substantial increase in glucose uptake, enabled by rapidly increased GLUT1 on cell membrane, that dominates the simultaneous increase in gross glycogen cycling capacity.

Shifts in nutrient utilization impact neutrophil functions in a function-specific manner: oxidative burst depends on glucose utilization, whereas NETosis and phagocytosis can be flexibly supported by either glucose or glycogen, and neutrophil migration and fungal control are enhanced by the shift from glycogen utilization to glucose utilization.

screening_protocol.order: All six fixed pairs, positive then distinct control; all six are mandatory, with no enrollment, post-result substitution, or cherry-picked triplet.
screening_protocol.no_screen_needed: The v5 source set uses all listed inputs. No validator eligibility/performance claim or query experiment has occurred.
screening_protocol.comparison_gate: The separate fourth-study protocol novelty-result-conditioned-pilot-prereg-v4.json must be committed with exact current runner/model/MCP/prompt/request hashes before any model or maintained-tool request.

criteria.primary: Across the six positive drafts, compare exact target-PMID coverage in shared-first-search union candidate-follow-up results against the matched shared-first-search union static-follow-up results. Candidate must cover at least one additional positive target in aggregate and lose none of the positive target coverage in static. A target already present in shared-first search cannot earn incremental credit by reappearing in either follow-up.
non_regression: Candidate loses none of the six distinct-control own-anchor coverage in matched shared-first-search union static-follow-up results, evaluated against shared-first-search union candidate-follow-up results.
Candidate does not increase cross-pair positive-target coverage among distinct controls; deduplicate each shared-first-search union follow-up PMID set identically for both arms.
Candidate does not increase the blinded unrelated-paper fraction among returned follow-up papers; incomplete blind labels make the outcome inconclusive.
Every returned paper has complete query, selected relaxation rung, selected/fetched/final PMID, source/tool, and actual server-process provenance.
criteria.shared_first_search_scoring: The identical shared-first-search set enters both arm coverage unions. Follow-up hits already present in that shared set cannot contribute an incremental gain or loss. Keep returned follow-up-paper blinded unrelated fractions as separately declared; no packet item may be missing a blind label.
criteria.failure_interpretation: A primary or non-regression failure rejects this exact frozen adaptation only. It does not establish that every iterative search method fails.
criteria.pass_interpretation: A pass retains the mechanism as promising only; no product adoption or release until the separately preregistered independent three-pair confirmatory comparison passes.
criteria.prospective_clarification: Independent review before the earlier study found that counting a follow-up re-retrieval of a seed target could fabricate incremental prior-art discovery. Union/dedup prevents this, retaining the original at-least-one improvement/no-loss/control/provenance thresholds.
